identity.title: Self-adaptive polynomial mutation in NSGA-II
identity.qualifying_affiliation: Universidad Nacional de Educacion a Distancia (UNED), Madrid, Spain

selected_variant: NSGA-II with self-adaptive polynomial mutation (NSGA-II + SA-PLM)

dynamic_controls.level: individual strategy state stored in the genome
dynamic_controls.application: used by polynomial mutation for each generated child
dynamic_controls.strength_mapping: lower eta_m produces broader and larger perturbations; higher eta_m produces narrower and smaller perturbations
dynamic_controls.feedback_path: NSGA-II rank and crowding selection -> selected parent eta_m values -> inheritance and Gaussian variation -> child mutation -> objective evaluation -> survivor selection

static_controls.parent_and_survivor_selection: fixed NSGA-II non-domination rank and crowding-distance rules

feedback_classification.explanation: The Gaussian perturbation is embedded in an inherited strategy variable whose propagation is controlled by current NSGA-II parent and survivor selection.

auxiliary_preference.note: Decision-vector dimension is not reinterpreted as a count of other parameters.

claim_boundary.detailed_method_source: Author's UNED-hosted 2022 method document that precedes the 2023 article

locators: PDF page 19: fixed controls and eta_m bounds
